title: Local observable errors from truncating interaction tails in gapped quantum lattice systems
abstract: We bound the error in ground-state expectations of local observables caused by truncating the spatial tails of a gapped quantum lattice Hamiltonian. We show that the error is controlled by the interaction strength discarded near each site, rather than by the extensive norm of the omitted Hamiltonian. If the gap remains open along a path that removes the interaction tail, the resulting bounds are uniform in system size and extend, under suitable assumptions, to thermodynamic-limit ground states. The convergence rate reflects the decay of the interaction tail: it is algebraic for power-law interactions, superpolynomial for superpolynomial interactions, and exponential at any strictly smaller rate for exponentially decaying interactions. For superpolynomial interactions, we also derive a direct infinite-volume estimate using automorphic equivalence. The results extend to isolated low-energy sectors and parity-even fermionic systems. For two-body interactions decaying as $r^{-p}$ in $d$ dimensions, we prove an error bound $O(R^{-(p-d)})$ for $p>2d$, where $R$ is the truncation range. We construct a gapped non-translation-invariant example that saturates this scaling, showing that the bound is optimal for the general class considered. Our results quantify when finite-range truncations faithfully reproduce the local physics of gapped long-range systems.
summary: This paper rigorously quantifies the error when approximating the physics of gapped quantum lattice systems by cutting off long-range interactions. It establishes that the convergence rate depends precisely on how fast the interaction tails decay, providing crucial theoretical bounds for simulating real-world materials or atomic arrays with long-range forces.
main_problem: The core problem is bounding the error incurred when approximating the ground-state expectation values of local observables in gapped quantum lattice systems by truncating the long-range spatial tails of the interaction Hamiltonian.
main_result: The error bound depends on the decay rate of the discarded interaction tail, yielding specific scaling laws (e.g., $O(R^{-(p-d)})$ for power-law interactions) that quantify when finite-range truncations accurately reproduce local physics.
method: The analysis employs spectral flow techniques, adiabatic path arguments, and rigorous bounding using localized seminorms to compare expectations between the full and truncated Hamiltonians in various limits (finite volume, thermodynamic limit).
model_or_system: The study concerns gapped quantum lattice systems whose interactions $\Phi$ decay spatially. The Hamiltonian is approximated by retaining only interactions within a finite range $R$, leading to the comparison between the full system and the truncated version.
key_observables: Error in ground-state expectation values of local observables ($\omega(A)$); Interaction Tail Mass ($T_{\Phi}(R)$).
important_parameters: Interaction decay rate (algebraic, superpolynomial, exponential); Truncation range $R$; System dimensionality $d$.
main_assumptions: The system must be gapped, and the existence of suitable adiabatic paths or common separating gaps is crucial for establishing uniform bounds.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the decomposition of the full interaction into retained bonds ($\Phi_{\le R}$) and the omitted tail ($\Phi_{>R}$) in a 2D lattice setting.
paper_structure: The paper develops results across multiple theorems (III.4, III.5, III.6) covering finite-volume, thermodynamic-limit, and infinite-volume bounds, supported by detailed mathematical appendices detailing the necessary functional calculus and norm estimates.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous quantitative tools to handle long-range interactions in quantum many-body systems, which is essential for modeling physical platforms like dipolar gases or Rydberg arrays where interactions decay slowly but are not strictly short-ranged.
